note.question: When do public signals gradually reveal a seller’s private quality, buyers and sellers trade sooner, screen more safely, or strategically wait for a better informational and bargaining position?
note.overview: The paper experimentally tests a one-sided incomplete-information bargaining game in which an uninformed buyer repeatedly offers prices to a privately informed seller while public news gradually reveals seller quality. Its theoretical benchmark is a sequential equilibrium with strategic delay, screening, and price experimentation.

components.label: Stationary sequential equilibrium of the bargaining-with-news benchmark
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Stationary sequential equilibrium of the bargaining-with-news benchmark. Section 3 summarizes the unique sequential equilibrium without news and the stationary equilibrium with news. Below threshold β the buyer experiments with offers between V_L and K_H that only a low type accepts; at or above β the buyer offers K_H and both types accept.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The seller privately knows type. The buyer makes an initial offer and then frequent offers over a potentially infinite horizon. Between offers, public stochastic news arrives and rejected offers also update beliefs; the game ends when the seller accepts. Rejection is informative because low and high types accept offers differently.
